title: One Press, One Glass Block. How Many Pieces? 💥
description:
Comment A, B, C or D 👇 How many pieces did the press crush this glass block into? Pick before the force starts to climb!

A glass block sits under a hydraulic press and the force climbs on a gauge. The whole block breaks at 23 tons. A piece breaks in two when the force passes its strength, and the strength of a piece is the block's strength divided by the square root of its size, so a piece a quarter of the size needs twice the force. Every cut falls along a random line and every piece has its own small flaw. The press climbs to 225 tons, then slams to 450 tons, twice that, and every piece that is weaker than the slam breaks, generation after generation. The piece counter always shows the real count. A band is crossed out the moment the count passes its top edge: A under 260 pieces, B 260 to 329, C 330 to 399, D 400 and up. The band that holds the final count wins. Double the force gives about four times the pieces. A simplified 2D toy model, not real glass physics.
Everything here is generated by code (seed 600), with no footage, samples or stock media.
Got it right? +1 streak. Which band did you pick?
#simulation #satisfying #crush
